scenes.heading: URL Parameters, Headers, TTL and Authentication
scenes.narration: Dispatcher. URL Parameters, Headers, TTL and Authentication. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the recommended /ignoreUrlParams strategy when most query parameters should not prevent caching?
scenes.heading: Ignore all parameters first, then deny only the ones that must bypass the cache
scenes.body: The speech recommends an allowlist approach: ignore everything with an allow rule on *, then deny only parameters that must bypass the cache, such as nocache.

Ignore all parameters first, then deny only the ones that must bypass the cache. scenes.question: A request URL has three query parameters, and one of them is not ignored by /ignoreUrlParams. What happens?
scenes.heading: If any parameter is not ignored, the page is not cached
scenes.body: The source says that if all parameters are ignored, the page is cached, but if any parameter is not ignored, the page is not cached.

scenes.question: What is the purpose of the /headers property in the Dispatcher cache configuration?
scenes.heading: /headers tells Dispatcher which response headers to store with the cached file and add back later
scenes.body: The speech says /headers lists the response headers Dispatcher stores next to the cached file and adds on later responses.
scenes.narration: What is the purpose of the /headers property in the Dispatcher cache configuration? /headers tells Dispatcher which response headers to store with the cached file and add back later. scenes.question: What must be done if a project wants Dispatcher to store ETag values for cached responses?
scenes.heading: Add ETag to /headers and set the Apache directive FileETag none
scenes.body: The speech explicitly says that to store ETag, you must add it to /headers and set the Apache directive FileETag none.

scenes.question: How does Dispatcher implement time-based invalidation when /enableTTL is set to 1?
scenes.heading: Dispatcher reads Cache-Control max-age or Expires and creates an auxiliary file whose mtime equals the expiry
scenes.body: The speech says /enableTTL reads Cache-Control max-age or Expires from the backend response and creates an empty auxiliary file whose modification time equals the expiry.

scenes.question: What does /allowAuthorized control?
scenes.heading: /allowAuthorized controls whether requests carrying authentication information may be cached
scenes.body: The speech says /allowAuthorized controls whether requests with authentication information are cached, including the Authorization header and cookies named authorization or login-token.

scenes.question: Why must /allowAuthorized remain 0 when Dispatcher session management is used?
scenes.heading: Session management requires /allowAuthorized to stay at 0
scenes.body: The source explicitly states that session management requires /allowAuthorized to be 0.
